frames.title: Step 1: Prepare the Python environment
frames.logic: I install the packages listed in the next cell once in the same environment as the notebook. In Jupyter or Colab, remove the comment marker from the installation line below if a package is missing. NumPy stores arrays and evaluates numerical operations. Matplotlib displays plots. Pillow reads and writes images. This installation does not change the model parameters.
frames.code:
# %pip install numpy "pillow>=10.1" matplotlib
import numpy as np
assert np.isfinite(np.array([0.0, 1.0])).all()
print("NumPy is ready:", np.__version__)

frames.title: Step 2: Read the image and check its dimensions
frames.logic: I download my public portrait once, or replace this path with my own image. An RGB array has two position axes and one channel axis. The three channels are red, green and blue.
frames.code:
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.request import urlretrieve

work = Path("lesson-data")
work.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

def get_file(relative_path):
    # I download a public example only when its local copy is missing.
    destination = work / Path(relative_path).name
    if not destination.exists():
        urlretrieve("https://saswataiith.github.io/" + relative_path, destination)
    return destination

portrait = get_file("assets/images/saswata-landscape.png")
output = "portrait-dynamics-results"

frames.title: Step 3: Prepare the next part of the calculation
frames.logic: I define the following operations. These are the same operations as in the original source, written on separate lines so their order is clear. Inspect their values before running the next cell.
frames.code:
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

frames.title: Step 4: A portable display font
frames.logic: I try the original font, then DejaVu Sans, then Pillow's default font. The font changes labels on the image only; it does not change a numerical field.

frames.title: Step 5: Set up the Fourier grid
frames.logic: I construct Fourier wave numbers from the grid spacing and domain size. A Laplacian multiplies each Fourier mode by minus its squared wave number. The zero Fourier mode represents the spatial mean.
frames.code:
out = Path(output)
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
u = np.array(Image.open(portrait).convert('L').resize((256, 256)), float) / 127.5 - 1
ac = u.copy()
ch = u.copy()
mean0 = u.mean()
del u
k = 2 * np.pi * np.fft.fftfreq(256)
k2 = k[:, None] ** 2 + k[None, :] ** 2

frames.title: Step 6: Prepare the next part of the calculation
frames.logic: I define `dt`, `kap`, `S`, `font`, `small`, `records`. These are the same operations as in the original source, written on separate lines so their order is clear. Inspect their values before running the next cell.
frames.code:
dt = 0.1
kap = 0.4
S = 2
font = portrait_font(27)
small = portrait_font(23)
records = []

frames.title: Step 7: Define the energy diagnostic
frames.logic: I calculate the bulk and gradient contributions in the same convention as the source program. Fourier normalization is part of this definition. I compare this quantity through time within one model; energies from different functionals need not have the same meaning.
frames.code:
def energy(a):
    return np.mean((a * a - 1) ** 2 / 4) + kap / 2 * np.sum(k2 * abs(np.fft.fft2(a)) ** 2) / 256 ** 4

frames.title: Step 8: Advance the field and record the result
frames.logic: I apply the update in its original order. I record the mean, energy or other diagnostics at the specified intervals. I do not clip the numerical field. A saved picture is a display of the field, not a substitute for a conservation check.
frames.code:
for step in range(2001):
    if step % 25 == 0:
        i = step // 25
        im = Image.new('RGB', (1160, 730), '#f5f7f2')
        d = ImageDraw.Draw(im)
        d.text((24, 15), 'ONE FACE, TWO EVOLUTION LAWS', font=font, fill='#173d40')
        d.text((24, 52), f'Forward simulation | time {step * dt:.1f} | no target image or fidelity term', font=small, fill='#173d40')
        for x, a, title in [(24, ac, 'Allen-Cahn: nonconserved'), (604, ch, 'Cahn-Hilliard: conserved')]:
            d.text((x, 99), title, font=small, fill='#173d40')
            im.paste(Image.fromarray(np.uint8(np.clip((a + 1) * 127.5, 0, 255))).resize((528, 528)), (x, 139))
            d.text((x, 685), f'Mean field: {a.mean():+.5f} | change: {a.mean() - mean0:+.5f}', font=small, fill='#173d40')
        im.save(out / f'frame-{i:03d}.png')
        records.append([step * dt, ac.mean(), ch.mean(), energy(ac), energy(ch)])
    if step == 2000:
        break
    ac = np.fft.ifft2((np.fft.fft2(ac) - dt * np.fft.fft2(ac ** 3 - ac - S * ac)) / (1 + dt * (S + kap * k2))).real
    ch = np.fft.ifft2((np.fft.fft2(ch) - dt * k2 * np.fft.fft2(ch ** 3 - ch - S * ch)) / (1 + dt * k2 * (S + kap * k2))).real

frames.title: Step 9: My check of this result
frames.logic: I check finite values, conservation or the known reference result as specified below. An assertion stops the notebook if the condition fails. Inspect the quantities and tolerance rather than suppressing a failure.
frames.code:
assert np.isfinite(ac).all() and np.isfinite(ch).all()
assert abs(ch.mean() - mean0) < 1e-10
np.savetxt(out / 'diagnostics.csv', records, delimiter=',', header='time,AC_mean,CH_mean,AC_energy,CH_energy', comments='')
print('Initial/final mean:', mean0, ac.mean(), ch.mean())
